resolved_consensus_constraints.constraint: subjective perfect understanding is not machine-provable
process guard is not real-runtime or prod-readiness proof

accepted: Make the user-supplied lifecycle permanent through a local project document.
Require a machine-readable workflow attestation artifact.
Implement the guard as Rust audit tooling with positive and negative fixtures.
Integrate the guard into handoff-check and ship-readiness, not mvp-check.
Keep CHIMERA safety, MVP-scope, secrecy and Lab-vs-Real-World rules above the lifecycle.
rejected: Markdown-only process rule, because it would not force future sessions to leave machine-checkable evidence.
Claiming literal 100 percent subjective understanding, because it cannot be verified by files, hashes, commands or exit codes.
Using the lifecycle to expand MVP into post-MVP research fabric work.
risks_processed: Subjective words such as best, complete and fully understood are bounded by evidence-backed fields.
Lab/source process PASS is not promoted to real-world or production-readiness PASS.
Council and red-team participation are required in the attestation.
Sensitive stand, secret and payload data are rejected by the guard.

spans.required_proof: council roles must examine non-software disciplines and transferable fundamental principles
transfer checks must record properties, invariants, constraints, benefits, risks and tradeoffs
analogies must be checked and irrelevant analogies rejected with reasons
research planning must include interdisciplinary search before research starts
research must not be limited to software engineering
selected and rejected disciplines must be recorded with result or non-applicability reason
research must look for fundamental principles, not copy implementations
each transferred principle must list invariants, constraints, adaptable and non-transferable parts, benefits and risks
analogical ideas must be evaluated and weak or irrelevant ones rejected

items: • what fundamental properties make it successful;
• which parts of the principle can be transferred;
• what advantages the transfer will bring;
• what new risks the transfer creates.
• How would a mathematician solve this problem?
• How would a physicist solve it?
• How would a chemist solve it?
• How would a biologist solve it?
• How would an information theorist solve it?
• How would a cryptographer solve it?
• How would a specialist in distributed systems solve it?
• How would an aerospace engineer solve it?
• How would a spacecraft engineer solve it?
• How would a systems engineering specialist solve it?
• How would a fault‑tolerance specialist solve it?
• How would an operations researcher solve it?
• How would an economist solve it?
• How would a specialist in collective behaviour solve it?
• What analogous problems have already been solved in other fields of science?
• What fundamental principles made those solutions successful?
• Which of these principles can be safely transferred to the current problem?
